text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Germany's Minister of Foreign Affairs Klaus Kinkel said in a column that the common European currency, the euro, should be implemented as planned on January 1, 1999, to enable Europe to play in the first division in the world's economy.

- Maximum rents for new public housing apartments should be lowered to 800 crowns per square metre annually from 1,100, a government commission said. But property owners are protesting and say the current level should be raised.

- Confidence in social benefits, and thereby in the minority Social Democratic government, is shaky, said several Social Democratic parliament members in a letter to Minister of Social Affairs Maj-Inger Klingvall. The members called for more money for public benefits.
- Swedish umbrella labour union LO will make a last attempt to make member unions back a proposal about wage setting.
- Sweden's new car sales will rise until the year 2003 when sales volumes will reach 300,000 cars, Retail and Wholesale Research Institute HUI forecast.

- Swedish travel agents are looking into possibilities to stop Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) from lowering their ticket commissions. SAS cut commissions to five percent from between eight and nine percent.

- Mining and rubber company Trelleborg's board has forbidden company president Kjell Nilsson from accepting a seat on the board of state-owned power company Vattenfall, Minister of Industry & Commerce Anders Sundstrom said.

- Swedes are getting ready to trade in their old cars for shiny new models with Swedish car sales expected to increase steadily every year up to the year 2002 when 300,000 new cars will be sold, Retail and Wholesale Research Institute HUI said.
- Several hundred thousand of Ericsson's new cellular phone, the tiny GF 788, have already been sold. Demand is being created with the help of a 300 million crown marketing campaign.
